doc.title: Tom Varner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 13, 2025

chapter: Writing for horn, politics and creativity
title: Working away from the instrument, Covid, and retirement plans
summary: He has little bandwidth during full-time teaching and Covid, now retired and planning more large-ensemble writing like Nine Surprises; mentions Jamie Baum.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you ever get away from your music room, your piano, your horn, and just walk and work on ideas? Even not on purpose.

Yeah. Yeah. I have been doing that a little bit more. It’s been hard to like (a) teach in college full time; (b) teach in college full time then with the Covid days and that really took a lot to just keep your spirits up to then be super creative in the middle of all of that. Some people have been. My hat is off to them. A lot of my friends, I don't know if you know the flute player/composer Jamie Baum. She’s somebody you might want to interview. She has this great record out that’s based on sort of modern American poetry but it’s with this sort of octet and there’s you know Adrienne Rich or somebody else, but with great players. But she was stuck in Manhattan in a high rise, sometimes didn’t get out for weeks. It was horrible. So she’s like, “All right, I got to do something.” So she wrote this beautiful suite of pieces. But she was not teaching full time and she didn’t have kids. But she made great use of that time in that way. But once Covid was over, and I’m trying to think, then I got back to teaching more in person, which was great. But it’s just been hard to have the bandwidth and the brain power to like work on these big ideas. But I could do a lot of shorter improv-oriented pieces. And then I got the sabbatical and that’s been wonderful. But now I’ve retired. Now I do, I feel like okay I – so if I’m walking outside with no headphones, no music, no nothing, no agenda, I’m like saying okay, okay, if I have three saxes and three brass and I would have them do this and I could have them do this – more along the lines of “Heaven and Hell.” Or the other one called “Nine Surprises,” which is kind of like “Heaven and Hell Part 2” a little bit more optimistic, not quite so dark. So now I am starting to do that, and I need to, starting like today, get to that more. I’m like, well you might be finding out too – you’re not completely retired because you’re doing this job as a half-time job. But still if you have more free time on your hands you’re like okay now I can utilize the bandwidth that is now just freed up to do some of these other things, and I really do want to. Yeah.
